text.p: Earnings per share n/a n/a 0.39 Loss-0.15

Elite, a maker of food products, mainly coffee and chocolates, said the 16.6 percent decline in sales last year was mainly due to the closing and selling off of production lines in Europe as part of a company reorganisation.
Revenues were also hurt by the appreciation of the Israeli shekel against European currencies, the company said.
Revenues from Elite's overseas operations fell 27.4 percent last year to 909.9 million shekels. Domestic sales fell by 5.1 percent to 1.12 billion shekels.
The company noted that gross margins had improved last year to 24.3 percent from 21.2 percent in 1995. Operating margins held steady at about 3.6 percent.

Costs connected with Elite's reorganisation fell to 20.55 million shekels from 57.62 million in 1995. However, Elite took almost the entire 1996 charge in the fourth quarter, which left it with a loss for the period.
